key_insight: Bulk, phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6—the long-sought lead-free iodide double-perovskite—was synthesized for the first time in both microcrystal and thin-film form via halide exchange from Cs2AgBiBr6.
engineering_relevance: This enables a new stable, lead-free absorber candidate for solar and optoelectronic devices, with demonstrated film photoconductivity showing charge generation and transport.
method: Start with phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 microcrystals or evaporated films
Eliminate trace moisture to enable complete Br→I anion exchange
Verify phase purity, optical bandgap, PL, stability, and photoconductivity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports broad visible absorption with a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-IR photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, months-long stability in inert/dry air, and measured photoconductivity in films.
watch_item: The material is synthesized by indirect halide exchange from a bromide precursor, so scalable process control and residual moisture management may be critical for reproducibility.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
